candidates.exact_span: 4Q3             Lowest four-day average flow rate expected to occur once every three-years
candidates.computation_change_reason: Flow-based effluent limits and conditional monitoring triggers elsewhere may key off this specific 4Q3 statistic; a different reading of what flow rate or recurrence interval counts as 4Q3 would change which numeric limit applies (A) and whether flow-conditioned monitoring was required (B).

If BMP obligations elsewhere are interpreted as 'plan' versus the more common 'practice,' the scope of required BMP-related monitoring or conditional sampling could be classified differently for monitoring-obligation evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: BOD             Biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Numeric BOD limits apply only to the defined five-day test unless another duration is specified; interpreting 'unless noted otherwise' differently would change which reported BOD values are comparable to the applicable enforceable limit.

candidates.exact_span: CBOD            Carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: CBOD compliance comparisons depend on the five-day test definition and any exceptions signaled by 'unless noted otherwise'; alternate readings would change which CBOD measurements are eligible for limit comparison.

Critical dilution is used in deriving or applying dilution-dependent numeric limits; a different interpretation of CD would change the calculated or applicable enforceable limit used in exceedance analysis.

Whether submitted evidence counts as the required DMR affects whether monitoring obligations are met (B) and whether a missing ordinary numeric result should be treated as documented no-data versus inadequate evidence of required monitoring (C).

Limits sourced from ELGs versus other bases carry different numeric values and applicability rules; interpreting which requirements are ELG-based changes which enforceable numeric limit is selected for comparison.
Many numeric limits are expressed in mg/l; misinterpreting reported or limit units would change whether a measurement is treated as exceeding the applicable enforceable limit.
Trace-parameter limits may be stated in ug/l while other results are in mg/l; unit interpretation directly affects numeric limit applicability and exceedance determination.

Values reported below the method minimum level may be non-quantitative for compliance comparison (A) and classified as a documented no-data or not-required state rather than a violation or ordinary numeric result (C).

MQL is distinct from ML and governs when a result is considered quantified; different interpretations of MQL versus detection/reporting thresholds change limit comparability (A) and missing-evidence classification for sub-MQL results (C).

Reasonable-potential findings can trigger stricter limits or additional monitoring elsewhere; interpreting RP status differently would change which numeric limits apply (A) and which monitoring was required (B).
pH limits are compared in standard units rather than mg/l; treating pH results or limits under a different unit convention would change exceedance outcomes.
TMDL-derived allocations can establish or constrain numeric discharge limits; interpreting TMDL applicability or allocation method differently would change the enforceable limit used in comparison.

WET requirements involve non-numeric pass/fail or specific toxicity endpoints and associated monitoring schedules; interpreting what constitutes WET compliance changes both limit comparison treatment (A) and whether WET monitoring was required (B).
WLA sets facility-specific pollutant allocations that translate into numeric limits; a different reading of WLA scope or allocation basis would change the applicable enforceable limit.
